pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only an action

2. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Play: Structure and Setting.

3. When practising Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

4. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

5. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library?

6. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

7. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

8. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. No full stops

9. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. quickly

10. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

11. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. goes

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Impromptu Speeches and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 10.2.1 Note Making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Determiners: Numerals and Ordinals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

5. D — Where is the library?

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

8. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

9. C — run

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

11. B — went

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Impromptu Speeches; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 10.2.1 Note Making; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Determiners: Numerals and Ordinals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
